classification_reasons: Blast radius: plugin/gate/checks.py's lesson_and_eval/_supersedes_problem gates every entry_route:incident change at gate (e) for every project on this plugin version going forward, and plugin/lessons/index.py is a new generated-index subsystem that /sdlc-deploy and /sdlc-maintain both now depend on -- several independent, load-bearing pieces of behavior, not a small patch.

The spec reopened one concern mid-review (the Windows newline/CRLF mechanism) and this phase's fix rounds surfaced a real security fix (PR #132's supersedes path-traversal/absolute-path hardening) plus a process defect (a double iteration bump past the non-routine cap) -- not a tight, single-pass spec.

New, previously-uncovered code paths (supersedes path/shape validation, frontmatter bad-field-shape handling, non-UTF-8 lesson files) were added with new tests in recent rounds, which is exactly the kind of change existing tests did not already cover before this change.
attempted: Intent: confirmed no source file changed since the last continue verdict (106818d, and the continue re-affirmed at b508863c03); the two commits since then (b508863, b335a2f) only corrected fix-response.md's Round 4 narrative and re-ran the review pass. The change's purpose (frontmatter + generated lessons index + gate check) is unchanged and matches intent.md/spec.md throughout.

Spec and plan: unchanged this round; every requirement and fail case already traced to spec.md/plan.md citations in prior rounds; all Flagged concerns in spec.md remain [x] closed with a decision; plan.md's file list and order of work match the diff's file set (diff-e.patch --stat: artifacts.py, checks.py, index.py, the two command files, template/README.md, template/sdlc.yaml, docs/OPERATING_MODEL.md, the two manifests, and the three test files -- all named in plan.md).

Proof -- re-verified the specific claim this round's corrected fix-response.md makes (that three drafted edits to artifacts.py:89, checks.py:1637 and docs/OPERATING_MODEL.md:144 were reverted before commit, rather than landed silently): read the current on-disk text of all three files directly (not just the narrative). plugin/gate/artifacts.py:89 still reads '...lesson and eval (change 0003...'; plugin/gate/checks.py:1637 still reads '...its lesson and its eval (spec.md change 0003)'; docs/OPERATING_MODEL.md:144 still reads 'a heading per tag' -- none shows the drafted rewording ('eval case', 'a heading per class'). hook-log.jsonl independently confirms three Edit-tool invocations at 2026-10-08T11:38:30-37Z on exactly those three files, consistent with a draft-then-revert rather than no activity at all. review-findings.json (head b335a2f137, matching this HEAD) reports 0 Important and 5 nits, all previously-seen, doubt-stated items (unescaped markdown chars in generated links, non-string supersedes silently treated as absent, build()'s mkdir side effect on read-only check(), the README's missing sources run-<n> example, and the 'heading per tag' vs 'first tag' wording) -- none rises to Important under REVIEW.md's bar (would break behavior, leak data or breach a policy); none is a fix-type change touching a pre-existing test (change_type is feature). test.log/build.log/lint.log remain 'deferred to the runner' (no code changed this round, so no new run is expected); verifier.md is the earlier 00ddfc7 round's report, which is the correct round to stand on since no code this round's two commits touched is exercised by it.

Blast radius: no guardrail file (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, this repo's root sdlc.yaml) touched by either of the two commits since the last continue. template/sdlc.yaml and docs/OPERATING_MODEL.md are plugin-shipped/process-documentation content, not this repository's own guardrails (CLAUDE.md's explicit list), consistent with intent.md's 'Framework change: yes'. No sdlc.yaml risk_list item applies.

Policies: security-baseline and data-conventions skills re-read for this pass -- the supersedes hardening (bare-filename match, no parser-error leakage) already closes the one finding that would have been a real security/injection concern (PR #132); the remaining nits are style/robustness, not policy breaches. No new stored personal or sensitive field. definition-of-done's split (deterministic gate enforces; eval-case content quality stays advisory) is unchanged and explicitly settled in spec.md's Flagged concerns.

Tests: this round (the two commits since the last continue) added no test and claims no code change; the hook-log evidence confirms the one drafted-but-reverted edit attempt never reached a commit, so no pre-existing test was weakened and no new code path was left untested.
